Neha — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions before we lock the pilot MAP:

Summary of needs (from today):
- Streaming-first UX: token-by-token latency matters for our customer-facing chat (we measured perceived latency spikes above ~120ms).
- Latency targets: goal is p95 <= 50ms for ~512-token responses, p50 ~ 15–20ms.
- Concurrency: baseline 80 concurrent chats, burst to 200 for peak events.
- Throughput: sustained ~18k tokens/minute during business hours.
- Reliability/edge cases: graceful fallback to higher-latency model variant during overload; streaming resume on transient failures.

Attached is an initial SLO matrix from our Ops team (finovia_slo_matrix.xlsx). Two asks before we confirm the MAP:
1) Can Redwood validate the p95 numbers with streaming enabled and KV cache warmed?
2) What pilot resource footprint do you recommend for a two-week pilot with our traffic shape?

Ellen — really helpful notes, thanks. Below is our proposed SLO checklist + concrete pilot asks so we can align on the MAP. I copied the engineering and sales leads.

Redwood proposed SLO checklist (pilot readiness):
- Latency: measure streaming token-to-token p50/p95 under production prompt set (target p95 <= 50ms for 512 tokens; p50 <= 25ms).
- Throughput & concurrency: sustain 80 concurrent sessions for 2 hours, support 200 concurrent bursts for at least 15 minutes without request Throttles.
- Stability: no more than 0.5% failed streaming sessions; successful resume on transient network errors within 1s.
- Quality regression: compare top-50 prompt outputs vs. baseline model; quality delta must be < 2% on selected metrics.
- Fallback behavior: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant with transparent notification to the client in <200ms when load triggers fallback.

Pilot configuration we propose to validate the above (summary):
- Model: open-llama-70b-ish variant we demoed (quantized Q4_0)
- Nodes: start with 3 x p4d-24-like instances (autoscaling off for controlled test)
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch latency 6ms; prefix cache warmed with canonical prompts
- Canary: 10% traffic slice for 72 hours before full pilot

Ellen/Neha — quick technical follow-up outlining what we need to validate the p95 streaming target and suggested resource footprint.

Key assumptions:
- Target p95 of 50ms assumes network RTT consistent with our hosted regions (~10–15ms median), KV cache warm, and batched attention kernels enabled.
- For 512-token average response length we see higher tail impact from batching spikes; we recommend max batch size such that batch latency <= 6ms to keep token latency bounded.

Pilot resource estimate (rough):
- 3 nodes p4d-24-equivalent with 8 inference workers each — target sustain ~15–20k tokens/min with headroom for burst to 30k tokens/min across cluster.
- If you require burst concurrency to 200 simultaneous active streaming sessions, we should provision a temporary burst pool (add 1–2 nodes) for the 15-minute peak windows.

Performance validation plan (two-week pilot):
1) Warm cache & short-run baseline: warm KV cache using canonical prompts for 2h.
2) Load sweep: step up concurrency (10, 25, 50, 80, 150, 200) and record token latency p50/p95, retry rates, and streaming session failures.
3) Stability window: 4-hour sustained run at 80 concurrent sessions, collect drop/reconnects and quality checks.
4) Canary rollback criteria: if p95 > 80ms or failure rate > 1% for 30m, rollback to lower-throughput model variant.

What we need from Finovia to get started:
- Representative 48–72hr traffic CSV (timestamp, sessions/sec, avg prompt length)
- Top 200 prompt set for quality checks (anonymized)
- Confirmation of region/data residency requirement (us-east1 preferred).

I attached a CSV with the resource estimate table for clarity. Happy to sync for 30m to walk through the plan.

Thanks — Vivek
